A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NP -completeness of a graph problem is not affected much by restricting its domain to planar or low degree graphs, or by allowing the edge weights to have only a few distinct values.
a number of problems are NP -complete even in graphs of low degree, or in graphs of low genus, or when their domains are further restricted in other ways.

The main takeaway from our work is that
NP -completeness is not necessarily a property of the problems but rather a property of the domains over which they are considered.
even when the domains of NP -complete graph problems are restricted to small graphs, the problems are still computationally intractable.
the NP -completeness of a problem is not always an indication that the problem is inherently hard to solve.
